The main risk is adoption: each subnet must opt in, and until paid usage grows the burn link is theoretical.

marketAlerts.change: Across Protocol's across.to domain hijacked to serve a wallet drainer
marketAlerts.summary: Across, a major cross-chain bridge, said an attacker took control of its across.to domain at about 18:45 UTC on Nov 10 (12:45 PM CST) through a social-engineering attack on its registrar, Namecheap, and replaced the site with a phishing page that asked visitors to sign token approvals and permits. Across said it was alerted within 15 minutes; SEAL911 got major wallets to flag the domain and Cloudflare later removed its DNS records. Across regained the domain at 01:16 UTC on Nov 11 (7:16 PM CST Nov 10), said smart contracts, API users and third-party integrations were unaffected, and promised to make affected users whole. Across has not published a loss total; security firm GoPlus estimated about $350,000 across six chains.
marketAlerts.why: No contracts were exploited, but it is a clear reminder that a bridge's web front end and domain registrar are attack surfaces in their own right. Anyone who connected a wallet or signed on across.to on Nov 10 should revoke those approvals; the estimated loss is well below the High threshold.

marketAlerts.change: Initia L1 still halted; losses now put at $3.27M after cloud-key compromise
marketAlerts.summary: Initia halted its Layer 1 at 06:18 UTC on Nov 10 (12:18 AM CST) after unauthorized transfers from the escrow accounts that hold assets bridged to its rollups. Its updated account says an attacker used a compromised Google Cloud key to run a command injection, obtain further cloud and GitHub credentials and forge withdrawals from five rollups, moving about $3.27 million out of L1 escrows, up from the ~$605,000 first reported. About $2.16 million of that is still frozen on the halted chain. Initia says it is rebuilding infrastructure in an isolated environment, hardening cloud and IBC controls and plans to fully restore affected assets, but has not given a restart date.
marketAlerts.why: This is Initia's second exploit in about three weeks, and it shows how a single leaked cloud credential can reach bridge escrows across several rollups. Losses remain below the ~$10M High threshold and no focus network is directly involved, so it stays Medium; the restart plan and asset restoration are the next things to watch.

marketAlerts.change: Arcus DEX on Robinhood Chain loses $2.23M to a subaccount accounting bug
marketAlerts.summary: Arcus, a perpetuals and tokenized-stock exchange on Robinhood Chain, said a newly created account exploited a subaccount-transfer accounting bug on Nov 9 that inflated its recorded balance, then withdrew $2,234,391 in USDG against it. Arcus paused withdrawals, patched the flaw and covered the shortfall from its treasury, and says a further ~$3 million in withdrawal requests was stopped by bridge rate limits and reversed. It reports other users' balances, positions and orders were unaffected and is working with investigators on recovery.
marketAlerts.why: Robinhood Chain is one of the newer homes for tokenized equities, so an early accounting failure on a venue there is worth noting, as is the role of bridge rate limits in capping losses. The treasury backstop means no user losses are reported, and the size is below the High threshold.

marketAlerts.change: Ankr's Ethereum cross-chain bridge exploited for about $0.3M
marketAlerts.summary: Blockaid flagged an ongoing exploit of Ankr's Ethereum cross-chain bridge at 2:42 AM CST on Nov 9: five withdrawals, referencing one small Optimism deposit, drained about $292,000 of locked assets (ankrETH, ankrPOL, ANKR and others) to a new wallet. SlowMist later put losses near $304,500 and said all five forged receipts carried valid signatures from the bridge's trusted signers; whether signer keys were compromised is still under investigation. Blockaid also reported the attacker swept several Ankr operator wallets on Ethereum, Arbitrum and Linea hours earlier. Ankr had not published a post-mortem at review time.
marketAlerts.why: The dollar loss is below the High threshold, but valid-signature forged receipts point at signer or key compromise rather than a simple contract bug, which is the failure mode that matters for every multisig-verified bridge. Exchanges paused related deposits as a precaution.

marketAlerts.change: LNbits tells every operator to shut down servers after fund-draining attacks
marketAlerts.summary: LNbits, the open-source Lightning wallet and accounts layer, told all operators on Nov 8 (7:56 AM CST) to stop their servers immediately after a wave of attacks, about 80 minutes after first warning Paywall-extension users. It disabled every instance on its hosted my.lnbits.com service and said services would resume within 24 hours, with patches expected in 24 to 48 hours. One operator (BitTipBot) reported 2,285,545 sats (about 0.023 BTC) withdrawn by newly created accounts before shutdown. LNbits has not disclosed the vulnerability, affected versions or a total loss figure.
marketAlerts.why: This is an application-layer incident, not a flaw in Bitcoin or the Lightning protocol, but LNbits sits behind many tipping bots, point-of-sale setups and custodial Lightning wallets, so a shutdown order affects a broad slice of small Lightning services. Confirmed losses so far are small; it stays Medium until patches ship and a total is known.

news.title: Helius launches Solana Privacy Rings on mainnet, bringing encrypted balances and private transfers
news.body: Helius released Solana Privacy Rings on Solana mainnet on Nov 10, and the Solana account amplified the launch as breaking news. The permissionless Ring is a shielded pool that encrypts asset types and amounts while leaving wallet addresses visible; only the owner can decrypt balances with a viewing key, every transaction still needs the owner's signature, and it supports SOL, SPL and Token-2022 assets. Helius says the programs and zero-knowledge circuits were audited by Certora, OtterSec and ZK Security, with formal verification expected to finish by the end of 2026. Decrypt's money account, Ore and Aurora Intents shipped integrations on day one, Range, Chainalysis and Elliptic support compliance screening, and Helius says Backpack, DFlow, Jupiter, Squads and Titan are integrating. Custom Rings for institutions, with KYC allowlists, auditor visibility and freeze controls, are still in audit and targeted for later in Q4 2026.
news.why: Confidentiality has been a gap for institutions and payments on public chains, and this adds it natively on Solana without moving funds to a separate network or slowing settlement. It is early: this release hides amounts rather than counterparties, the institutional version is not live yet, and real usage will show up only as integrators turn it on.
news.tagReason: A live, audited privacy layer on Solana mainnet with named day-one integrations.
news.summary: Helius released Solana Privacy Rings on Solana mainnet on Nov 10, and the Solana account amplified the launch as breaking news.

news.title: X cashtags now open trades in any Solana token through fomo, and OpenWorld puts its Nasdaq shares on Solana
news.body: From Nov 10, X users can tap a Solana token's cashtag to see live market data and open the fomo app to buy or sell it, with fomo handling execution from its self-custodial wallet; Solana's official account announced the feature at 8:15 AM CST. Reports say it covers all Solana tokens, including long-tail ones, but X does not run the exchange or hold funds, and availability by country and fees were not specified. Separately, Nasdaq-listed OpenWorld made its own shares (OPNW) available as tokens on Solana via the Sunrise platform, issued by Backpack Securities, without issuing new shares or raising capital. Solana's account posted both launches the same morning.
news.why: Putting a trade button on cashtags in one of the largest social apps is a major distribution channel for Solana's onchain markets, though it will skew to speculative tokens. The OpenWorld listing adds another real company to Solana's tokenized-equity shelf, a smaller step than Formation's venue but live today.
news.tagReason: A mass-market trading entry point and a new live tokenized equity on Solana.

news.title: Bittensor turns on Gamma Tokens, dollar-valued credits that let wallets and agents pay subnets directly
news.body: The Opentensor Foundation announced Gamma Tokens on Nov 10 as a native payment system for Bittensor: users and AI agents can pay for subnet services with a Bittensor wallet instead of separate accounts and API keys for each subnet. Gamma is minted by paying TAO (the protocol buys and burns that subnet's alpha) or by burning alpha directly, and each Gamma is worth $1 of service credit, priced through an onchain TAO/USD feed. Credits are specific to one subnet, cannot be transferred or redeemed back into TAO or alpha, and are spent through signed requests with spending limits. The mechanism merged in Runtime 488 on Nov 5 and was switched on network-wide late on Nov 9; trackers show Attune (SN58), Engy (SN53) and Terza Inference (SN103) enabling it first on Nov 10, with only about $0.42 of Gamma minted and spent by that evening.
news.why: Gamma gives Bittensor a direct link between paid demand for a subnet's product and its token, because every purchase burns alpha. It is a protocol-level step toward real revenue, but each subnet must opt in, and the first day's dollar volume was negligible.
news.tagReason: A live protocol payment layer tying subnet usage to alpha burns, though adoption is just starting.

news.title: Fidelity's FCAT becomes a required verifier for every Ondo Stocks cross-chain transfer
news.body: Ondo Finance said on Nov 10 that the Fidelity Center for Applied Technology (FCAT) is now a required verifier for Ondo Stocks moving between Ethereum, HyperEVM and other supported chains through the Ondo Bridge. FCAT's Decentralized Verifier Network validates each transfer alongside a quorum of other verifiers before it settles on the destination chain, covering 35 Ondo Stocks bridged to HyperEVM and all 450+ Ondo Stocks on other networks. The Ondo Bridge first adopted FCAT's verifier through LayerZero in February 2026; this extends it to the tokenized-stock line. Ondo says tokenized stocks now top $3 billion across chains, and transfers remain open only to eligible investors outside the US.
news.why: Having a Fidelity unit sign off on every cross-chain move adds institutional security to the bridge, which is the riskiest part of multichain tokenized assets. It strengthens Ondo's infrastructure story, but it is a security upgrade rather than new demand, and US investors still cannot use the product.
news.tagReason: A major TradFi institution now co-verifies every Ondo Stocks bridge transfer.

news.title: Flare fast-tracks an emergency hard fork after spotting an exploit attempt on its node software
news.body: Flare said on Nov 10 (1:49 PM CST) that it is rolling out go-flare v1.15.1, a mandatory hard fork that patches a vulnerability in the upstream Avalanche-based code its nodes run. The fix had been planned for later in November, but Flare brought it forward after its monitoring flagged an attempt to exploit the bug; Flare Devs called the attempt active and told all validators and node operators to upgrade first. The fork activates on Flare mainnet on Nov 11 at 14:00 UTC (8:00 AM CST), after Songbird at 08:00 UTC. Flare says user funds and keys are not affected and users need do nothing, while exchanges such as Poloniex are pausing FLR deposits and withdrawals around the upgrade. The GitHub release was rebuilt on Nov 11 after the first build failed at the Songbird and Coston activation; Flare-mainnet nodes were not affected by that bug.
news.why: A detected exploit attempt plus a rushed hard fork is a real operational risk for a network that sits under FXRP and Firelight. The quick response is reassuring, but the test is whether enough stake upgrades in time for a clean activation, and the Songbird rebuild shows how fast emergency releases can stumble.
news.tagReason: An exploit attempt forced an emergency fork, though Flare says no funds or keys are affected.
news.summary: Flare said on Nov 10 (1:49 PM CST) that it is rolling out go-flare v1.15.1, a mandatory hard fork that patches a vulnerability in the upstream Avalanche-based code its nodes run.

news.title: SEC lets Nasdaq ISE list options on qualifying digital-commodity ETPs without case-by-case approval
news.body: The SEC approved Nasdaq ISE's rule change SR-ISE-2026-42 on Nov 10, allowing the exchange to list options on commodity-based trusts that hold one or more digital commodities without a separate SEC approval for each product. A trust qualifies only if each asset averages at least $700 million in daily market value over 12 months and at least 85% of its net asset value sits in assets with surveillance-linked futures markets. Coverage of the order ties eligibility to the 19 assets the SEC and staff have identified as digital commodities, which include XRP, XLM, HBAR, DOT, ALGO, SOL and ETH. The order approves an options framework, not any new spot ETF; each underlying product still needs its own listing.
news.why: Listed options are what institutions use to hedge and size positions, so a standing framework makes future products on several focus assets easier to support. It is plumbing, not demand: smaller assets may fail the liquidity tests, and nothing new trades until a qualifying trust lists.
news.tagReason: A constructive regulatory framework step, with no product launch yet.
news.summary: The SEC approved Nasdaq ISE's rule change SR-ISE-2026-42 on Nov 10, allowing the exchange to list options on commodity-based trusts that hold one or more digital commodities without a separate SEC approval for each product.

news.title: XRPL Foundation's roadmap maps quantum-safe accounts that keep the same address and base fee
news.body: CoinDesk reported on Nov 10 on a design in the XRP Ledger Foundation's 2027 protocol roadmap, updated Nov 4, that would let account owners add a quantum-resistant ML-DSA-44 signing key (a NIST-approved scheme) and then disable the original key, with no new address, no moving funds and no higher base fee. The new signatures are bulky: about 3.6 KB extra per protected transaction, with the Foundation putting storage at 5,331 bytes per protected payment against a 1,704-byte baseline. The draft Quantum amendment has an implementation branch that has run on AlphaNet, but known issues remain, including a seed-derivation mismatch between implementations. The Foundation schedules a migration study in the first half of 2027, then development and audit in late 2027 or 2028, with a $215,000 to $255,000 review budget; Ripple targets a full transition by 2028 and no activation date is set.
news.why: Every account that has sent a payment has exposed its public key, so a clean migration path matters for the ledger's long-term security. This is a draft that still needs a validator vote, and owners would have to rotate keys themselves, so it reduces future risk only if people actually migrate.
news.tagReason: Concrete security planning, but a draft with no activation date.
news.summary: CoinDesk reported on Nov 10 on a design in the XRP Ledger Foundation's 2027 protocol roadmap, updated Nov 4, that would let account owners add a quantum-resistant ML-DSA-44 signing key (a NIST-approved scheme) and then disable the original key, with no new address, no moving funds and no higher base fee.

news.title: Polkadot Referendum 1966 enacts, putting the 500-validator target into effect
news.body: Polkadot's Referendum 1966 was enacted on Nov 10 at relay-chain block 33,814,400, a day earlier than the block-height estimate the dashboard carried. It sets a 500-validator target for the active set and trims the validator incentive budget proportionally; the new limit applies from the first era after enactment, so it was in force by about midday Nov 11. The referendum passed on Nov 7, so this is the execution step rather than a new decision.
news.why: Fewer active validators cut what Polkadot spends on security incentives, but they also reduce the number of independent operators. Watch whether stake concentrates among the remaining validators.
news.tagReason: A planned governance change executed on schedule.
news.summary: Polkadot's Referendum 1966 was enacted on Nov 10 at relay-chain block 33,814,400, a day earlier than the block-height estimate the dashboard carried.

news.title: DFINITY says Cloud Engines ship this week, with early-access coupons going out
news.body: DFINITY posted on Nov 10 that Dominic Williams has confirmed the release of Cloud Engines this week and that early-access coupons are being issued. A cloud engine is a business's own private Internet Computer subnet built from nodes it selects in a market, with its choice of hardware, location and security settings; Williams called it 'going to be the biggest thing in the history of the Internet Computer.' DFINITY has not published an exact date or pricing.
news.why: Cloud Engines are ICP's main attempt to sell sovereign cloud capacity to businesses, so a confirmed release turns a long-running pitch into a product. Until it ships and customers appear, it remains a launch promise.
news.tagReason: A confirmed near-term product release, not yet shipped.
news.summary: DFINITY posted on Nov 10 that Dominic Williams has confirmed the release of Cloud Engines this week and that early-access coupons are being issued.

news.title: LlamaRisk proposes narrowing Aave V3 Core to blue-chip collateral and moving restaking tokens to V4
news.body: Risk provider LlamaRisk posted an Aave governance proposal (ARFC) on Nov 10 to reposition Aave V3's Ethereum Core market around established, liquid collateral. It would freeze new supply on reserves such as rsETH, osETH and LBTC and coordinate an orderly migration of existing positions to Aave V4 or repayment, without forced liquidations; coverage puts the affected collateral at roughly $1.3 billion to $1.5 billion. WETH, WBTC and major stablecoins would stay in Core, and LBTC is expected to continue on a dedicated V4 spoke. The proposal is not in effect and has no vote date yet.
news.why: Aave is the largest lender on Ethereum, so tightening its main market reduces contagion risk from restaking and wrapped-BTC tokens. It could shrink demand for some ETH-based liquid restaking tokens in the near term, and the details depend on the vote and V4 timing.
news.tagReason: A prudent risk proposal for Ethereum's biggest lending market, still at the discussion stage.
news.summary: Risk provider LlamaRisk posted an Aave governance proposal (ARFC) on Nov 10 to reposition Aave V3's Ethereum Core market around established, liquid collateral.

news.title: AMD makes 6th Gen EPYC 'Venice' server CPUs generally available, with systems shipping now
news.body: AMD announced availability of its 6th Gen EPYC SP7 server processors on Nov 10, built on the new Zen 6 architecture and aimed at agentic AI, enterprise, cloud and HPC workloads. AMD says systems are already shipping from all leading server OEMs and ODMs, with Microsoft Azure and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure instances coming soon. It also launched EPYC Embedded 9006 parts with up to 256 cores, PCIe Gen 6 and CXL 3.1, and pointed to its Helion agentic AI rack as an open blueprint pairing the CPUs with GPUs. Performance claims in coverage are AMD's own and early third-party benchmarks.
news.why: AMD is betting that AI agents push more work back onto CPUs that orchestrate GPUs and run the databases agents query, and a shipping Zen 6 generation is its main vehicle for that. Broad OEM availability on day one matters more than benchmark claims for data-center share.
news.tagReason: A new flagship server CPU generation is generally available and shipping.
news.summary: AMD's Zen 6-based 6th Gen EPYC server CPUs are generally available, with OEM systems shipping and Azure/OCI instances coming.

sources.title: AMD Newsroom · 6th Gen EPYC now available (Nov 10)

news.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model, available to developers, enterprises and Ultra subscribers
news.body: Google DeepMind made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available on Nov 10, two weeks after giving it to cybersecurity defenders through its Fairwind Program. Google describes Carbon as its strongest model for long-horizon agentic work, complex coding and scientific reasoning, and positions it above Gemini 4 Argon for the hardest tasks. It is available through the Gemini API in AI Studio and Gemini for business at an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, rising to $4 and $20 after Nov 30, and is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, Antigravity and AI Mode in Search. Google also previewed a /swarm feature in Antigravity that runs coordinated teams of agents; benchmark rankings cited are Google's and its partners'.
news.why: A new top-tier model with aggressive introductory pricing is how Google competes for developer and enterprise AI spend, which drives demand for its TPUs and cloud. The price step-up after Nov 30 is the detail to watch for customer uptake.
news.tagReason: A generally available frontier model across Google's API, cloud and consumer products.
news.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Carbon broadly on Nov 10 via API, Gemini for business and Ultra subscriptions, with introductory pricing through Nov 30.

sources.title: Google · Gemini 4 Carbon is now available (Nov 10)

news.title: NVIDIA releases Alpamayo 2 Edge, an open 2B-parameter driving model built to run in the car
news.body: NVIDIA released Alpamayo 2 Edge on Nov 10, a 2-billion-parameter vision-language-action model that turns surround-camera video, motion history and navigation instructions into driving trajectories, generating step-by-step reasoning only when a scene needs it. NVIDIA says closed-loop reinforcement learning in its AlpaGym simulator improved driving performance by 48.9% over the best checkpoint without it, and that an optimized build runs at 160 to 190 milliseconds from pixels to trajectory on DRIVE AGX Thor. Weights are on Hugging Face, alongside an AlpaJudge model for scoring reasoning quality, and early partners PORT, Niulinx and Embedl reported running it within days. The performance figures are NVIDIA's and its partners' own.
news.why: Open, in-vehicle reasoning models make NVIDIA's DRIVE Thor hardware more attractive to automakers that do not build their own full self-driving stack, a different approach from Tesla's in-house FSD. It deepens NVIDIA's physical-AI push beyond data centers.
news.tagReason: A meaningful open model release for autonomous driving, with vendor-reported results.
news.summary: NVIDIA open-sourced Alpamayo 2 Edge, a compact driving model that runs in real time on DRIVE AGX Thor.

news.title: Elliptic: Binance-hack launderers minted throwaway NEAR memecoins to move about $430,000
news.body: Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reported that the North Korea-linked group behind Binance's Oct 29 hot-wallet breach created six throwaway memecoins on NEAR between Nov 5 and 7. It says about 117,000 NEAR (roughly $430,000) of stolen funds was swapped into the tokens through decentralized-exchange pools and then sold back for NEAR from separate wallets, hiding direct wallet-to-wallet links. The tokens saw no real trading and were abandoned, and Elliptic says the flows remain traceable.
news.why: NEAR's protocol was not attacked, but laundering through its DEX pools could invite more compliance scrutiny of NEAR liquidity and keep NEAR on exchanges' watchlists while Binance finishes reopening withdrawals.
news.tagReason: Stolen funds were routed through NEAR DEX pools, a reputational and compliance headache.
news.summary: Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reported that the North Korea-linked group behind Binance's Oct 29 hot-wallet breach created six throwaway memecoins on NEAR between Nov 5 and 7.

news.title: Update: HYPE won markets are now live on both Upbit and Bithumb
news.body: Following Upbit's listing notice covered in the last edition, Upbit opened HYPE trading against KRW, BTC and USDT at 3:00 PM KST on Nov 10 (12:00 AM CST), with deposits and withdrawals only via HyperEVM. Bithumb, Korea's second-largest exchange, added its own HYPE/KRW market later the same day. That gives Korean retail two domestic won routes into HYPE in one day.
news.why: Korea is one of crypto's biggest retail markets, and won pairs at both major exchanges widen HYPE's distribution beyond offshore venues. Whether this adds lasting liquidity is something only later volume data will show.
news.tagReason: Both top Korean exchanges now list HYPE in won.
news.summary: Following Upbit's listing notice covered in the last edition, Upbit opened HYPE trading against KRW, BTC and USDT at 3:00 PM KST on Nov 10 (12:00 AM CST), with deposits and withdrawals only via HyperEVM.

news.title: Acala and Karura propose shutting down on Feb 10, 2027
news.body: Acala announced on Nov 9 that it plans to wind down the Acala parachain on Polkadot and Karura on Kusama, and opened signalling referendums (Acala #195, Karura #137) to approve the plan. If they pass, withdrawals and XCM transfers stay open until Feb 10, 2027, when the chains stop producing blocks; LDOT must be unbonded by Jan 12 (Dec 16 for LDOT locked to specific validators) and LKSM by Feb 2. The team says it will try, as a last resort, to return leftover external assets to owners' Asset Hub accounts and donate treasury external assets to the Polkadot and Kusama treasuries. ACA and KAR cannot be withdrawn and stay on their chains. The team cites liquidity that never built up, fragmentation across parachains and usage that no longer covers running a dedicated chain.
news.why: Acala held Polkadot's first parachain slot and was its flagship DeFi hub, so its exit is a clear signal about parachain-era economics and DeFi fragmentation on Polkadot. DOT, USDT and USDC holders on Acala have firm deadlines, while the ecosystem's shift toward Asset Hub as the main liquidity venue continues.
news.tagReason: A founding Polkadot DeFi parachain is planning to shut down for lack of liquidity and usage.
news.summary: Acala and Karura propose a Feb 10, 2027 shutdown; LDOT unbonding deadlines start Dec 16.

news.title: NEAR AI pauses and restores its cloud after an SGLang-based intrusion
news.body: NEAR AI said on Nov 9 that it found unauthorized access to its internal systems and paused NEAR AI Cloud inference while it investigated. Its incident report says an attacker used a remote-code-execution flaw in SGLang, the open-source inference engine it runs, on Nov 8; about 100 users' account details were downloaded, 18 legacy agents' chat histories, settings and logs were accessed, and two Cloud API keys were exposed and revoked. NEAR AI patched every server, rotated credentials and brought the cloud back online late on Nov 9 CST. It says NEAR Protocol and other NEAR services were not affected.
news.why: NEAR is positioning private, user-owned AI as a core use case, so a breach of its AI cloud tests that pitch even though the chain itself was untouched. The fast disclosure and restoration limit the damage; the follow-up to watch is whether the report shows the enclave design kept customer prompts private.
news.tagReason: A confirmed security incident at NEAR's flagship AI service, though the protocol was unaffected.
news.summary: NEAR AI disclosed a Nov 8 intrusion via an SGLang flaw, paused NEAR AI Cloud and restored it; the protocol was unaffected.

news.title: AWS launches Nitro Sandboxes for hardware-isolated pods, tasks and AI agents
news.body: AWS said on Nov 9 that Nitro Sandboxes are now available as lightweight virtual machines managed by the Nitro Hypervisor, so each Amazon EKS pod, ECS task or lightweight VM, including AI agents, can run in its own hardware-isolated environment. AWS says workloads run at near-native EC2 performance and can be validated through cryptographic attestation, so secrets are released only to sandboxes that prove their integrity. Turning it on in EKS or ECS is described as a one-line change, and Amazon Linux and Firecracker are natively supported. It is available on most Nitro-based EC2 instances in all commercial regions at no additional charge.
news.why: Safely running untrusted, LLM-generated code is a core requirement for agentic AI, and AWS is building that isolation into its standard compute at no extra cost. It strengthens AWS's pitch for hosting AI agents and multi-tenant workloads, which matters for the AI and compute backdrop that decentralized compute networks compete against.
news.tagReason: A generally available, no-cost security feature aimed squarely at AI-agent workloads.
news.summary: AWS made Nitro Sandboxes generally available on Nov 9 for hardware-isolated EKS pods, ECS tasks and AI agents at no extra charge.

news.title: NVIDIA introduces GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0 at the Conference on Robot Learning
news.body: NVIDIA said on Nov 9 at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin that it is introducing GR00T 2, an open world action model for robots built on NVIDIA Cosmos and trained partly on 100,000 hours of open human egocentric data. NVIDIA reports it reached 71% average success across 50 tasks with one demonstration per task, rising to 95% with five; those are NVIDIA's own figures. It also released Isaac Lab 3.0, which it says delivers up to 2.5 times the training throughput of the prior version on one benchmark, plus new open benchmarks DexBench and VABAR. Foxconn, Siemens and Nexuni are named as testing or evaluating GR00T 2.
news.why: Robotics is one of NVIDIA's next demand stories beyond data-center training, and open models plus simulation tools pull developers onto its GPUs and software stack. Results are company-reported and early, so the signal is ecosystem momentum rather than revenue.
news.tagReason: A meaningful open-model and tooling release, with performance claims that are self-reported.
news.summary: NVIDIA unveiled the open GR00T 2 robot model, Isaac Lab 3.0 and new benchmarks at CoRL on Nov 9.

news.title: AMD EPYC CPUs host Google Cloud's TPU 8tx, the first cloud TPU with confidential computing
news.body: AMD said on Nov 9 that 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors power the host infrastructure for Google Cloud TPU 8tx, which both companies describe as the first cloud TPU system with hardware-enforced confidential computing. The EPYC chips handle orchestration, data preparation and communication with the TPUs, and AMD's Secure Encrypted Virtualization extends protection to the connected accelerators so prompts, model weights and intermediate data stay encrypted in memory and in transit. Google Cloud's Mark Lohmeyer is quoted saying this brings confidential computing to cloud TPUs for the first time. AMD also says EPYC is the host CPU for more than 10 leading hyperscalers and frontier AI labs.
news.why: It ties AMD's server CPUs into Google's in-house AI chip platform, not just GPU systems, and gives Google a security feature aimed at enterprises moving sensitive AI agents into production. Confidential AI compute is the same problem decentralized AI networks pitch to solve, so it is useful context for the AI and compute coins.
news.tagReason: A jointly confirmed product launch that expands both companies' AI infrastructure roles.
news.summary: AMD EPYC now hosts Google Cloud TPU 8tx, the first cloud TPU system with hardware-enforced confidential computing.

news.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, a low-cost model for high-volume agent work
news.body: Meta introduced Muse Ember on Nov 9, its smallest and most efficient model, built for repeated agent tasks such as tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction and long-document parsing. It is available on the Meta Model API and Muse Code at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window. Meta says it is the first model trained using Muse Wonder Full and cites Artificial Analysis results placing it on the cost-efficiency frontier; several comparisons are Meta's own evaluations. Box, Cline, Oracle, Cloudflare and You.com are quoted from early testing, and Meta says its Muse models are now available on Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud.
news.why: Meta is competing on price for the agent workloads that drive most AI token volume, and selling through other clouds widens its reach beyond its own apps. Cheaper agent models lower costs across the AI stack, which matters for the backdrop around decentralized AI and compute networks.
news.tagReason: A generally available paid model with named enterprise testers, though some benchmarks are self-reported.
news.summary: Meta launched Muse Ember on Nov 9, a low-cost agent model priced at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens.

news.title: Nvidia's board opens an independent investigation after reports Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort
news.body: Nvidia's board said on Nov 8 that independent directors, working with outside counsel, will oversee an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. In a company-wide email published by CNBC, Huang apologized to his family and employees for a personal relationship, said he would cooperate fully and reaffirmed his commitment to Nvidia and US national security. The board said it continues to support Huang's leadership while the review proceeds. Republican lawmakers had earlier asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on the matter, and the review's scope and timing have not been published.
news.why: This is a governance and policy-risk story for the most important AI-chip supplier, arriving days before Nvidia's Nov 17 results and amid tighter scrutiny of chip exports to China. Nvidia has no verified direct crypto exposure, so it matters here for the AI and compute backdrop rather than any watchlist network.
news.tagReason: A board-level investigation adds governance and regulatory uncertainty; no wrongdoing has been established.
news.summary: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation on Nov 8; Huang apologized to staff and said he will cooperate.

sources.title: CNBC · Huang email and board statement

researchSummary.body: The Nov 8–10 window leans constructive on product releases, with security cautions around the edges. Solana shipped a native privacy layer (Helius Privacy Rings) and a mass-market trading entry point through X cashtags, Bittensor switched on Gamma Tokens to tie subnet payments to alpha burns, and Fidelity's FCAT became a required verifier for Ondo's tokenized-stock bridge. Regulation moved in the background: the SEC cleared Nasdaq ISE to list options on qualifying digital-commodity ETPs, a framework that names XRP, XLM, HBAR, DOT, ALGO, SOL and ETH among eligible assets, and 21 banks committed about $270 million to Project Faro's dollar stablecoin for 2027. The cautions are Flare's emergency hard fork after an exploit attempt, laundering of Binance-hack funds through NEAR memecoins, and market-wide incidents at Across, Arcus, Initia and Ankr, none above the $10M High threshold. Nothing here implies a price outcome, and it is not financial advice.

weeklyRecap.title: Week in context · Nov 4–10, 2026
weeklyRecap.body:
The week's main theme was distribution moving into regulated and mainstream channels. Solana gained Formation's SEC-exemption notice for a tokenized-securities venue, a Schwab Crypto listing, a native privacy layer from Helius and one-tap trading from X cashtags; NEAR Intents went live in Talos's institutional system; HYPE gained won markets on Upbit and Bithumb plus the Elysium L2; and Ondo brought Fidelity's FCAT into every tokenized-stock bridge transfer. Bittensor's Gamma Tokens went live as a protocol payment rail, though first-day use was tiny.

Governance moved from votes to execution. Polkadot enacted Referendum 1966's 500-validator target on Nov 10, while Acala and Karura proposed shutting down in February 2027. Render's RNP-024 closed with only yes votes shown but no official announcement, and the XRPL Foundation's quantum-safe account design remains a draft with a 2027 study.

Security is the cross-watchlist caution. Flare forced an emergency hard fork after an exploit attempt, NEAR AI contained a cloud intrusion, and Elliptic traced Binance-hack laundering through NEAR memecoins. Market-wide incidents at Keplr/Web3Auth, LNbits, Ankr, Arcus, Initia and Across were each below the High threshold. Nothing in this recap is a price forecast or financial advice.

stocks.name: Tesla, Inc.
stocks.overview: Tesla builds electric vehicles and energy-storage systems and is investing heavily in self-driving (FSD, Robotaxi and the Cybercab), Optimus robots and its own AI compute. In Q3 2026 revenue was $28.05 billion, roughly flat year over year, with 486,532 deliveries (down about 2%) and net income attributable to common stockholders of $787 million ($0.22 per diluted share), down from $1.37 billion a year earlier; energy revenue fell 16% while services and other rose 33%. Recent moves include Cybercab service starting in Austin in September, a new €100 million Berlin engineering center that opened Nov 4 with about 250 staff, and an official Argentina launch set for Nov 20. Shareholders meet on Dec 3, and Tesla and SpaceX have discussed a possible combination, though no terms have been announced and any deal would need shareholder approval. The main near-term risk is political: after Democrats won Congress and Texas, Tesla and SpaceX shares fell about 11% and 9% on Nov 5, as investors priced in possible congressional probes and tighter rules on AI data centers.
stocks.researchSummary: Tesla's latest quarter showed flat revenue and lower profit, with a pivot in spending toward AI compute, robotaxis and robots. This week's company news was constructive (the Berlin engineering hub and the Argentina entry), but after the midterms the bigger story is the regulatory and political overhang on Elon Musk's companies.
stocks.cryptoLink: Tesla's Q3 2026 10-Q shows digital assets of $962 million at Sep 30, 2026, mostly 11,509 bitcoin acquired for $386 million, and the company booked a $288 million mark-to-market gain on its bitcoin in the quarter.

flags.text: CNBC reports that, with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress and Texas flipping, investors expect probes and steeper regulatory hurdles for Musk's AI and merger ambitions. Texas Gov.-elect Hinojosa has called for a moratorium on new data-center approvals.
Q3 automotive revenue fell 3% to $20.56 billion on lower average selling prices and battery-supply limits, and operating income dropped to $718 million from $1.62 billion as R&D spending rose 69%.

Tesla's strategy and its possible SpaceX combination both center on Elon Musk. CNBC notes he was the largest donor to GOP midterm candidates, most of whom lost, which ties Tesla's regulatory exposure to his political profile.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
stocks.overview: Meta runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, earns almost all of its revenue from advertising, and is spending heavily to build its Muse AI assistant and 'personal superintelligence'. Q3 2026 revenue rose 26% to $64.60 billion and diluted EPS was $3.83, or $7.40 excluding a $9.89 billion charge from its settlement with state attorneys general over teen mental health. Capital expenditures were $34.91 billion in the quarter and free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion. Meta expects 2026 capex of $135–145 billion and Q4 revenue of $73–76 billion. To fund the AI build-out it sold $15 billion of US-dollar bonds on Nov 3 and its first euro bonds (€9 billion) on Nov 4, and it has announced a non-voting Class C share class effective Jan 19, 2027. It launched Muse 'spaces' on Nov 6. The main risks are funding and returns on AI spending: S&P moved Meta's outlook to negative, and more youth-related trials are scheduled.
stocks.researchSummary: Meta's ad business is growing fast, but AI infrastructure spending has pushed free cash flow negative, so it is now raising large amounts of debt and planning equity. Product momentum in Muse continues, while litigation and data-center permitting after the midterms are the main watch items.
stocks.cryptoLink: Since April 2026, Meta has paid select creators in Colombia and the Philippines in Circle's USDC on Solana or Polygon via Stripe. It is not issuing its own stablecoin.

flags.text: Q3 included a $9.89 billion charge from a settlement with 52 state attorneys general of up to about $18.59 billion, and Meta says more youth-related trials are scheduled in the U.S. in the coming months.

Meta's capex of $135–145 billion turned Q3 free cash flow negative, S&P revised its outlook to AA- negative, and Meta's president said after the midterms that building data centers is 'going to be harder'.
Advertising was $63.06 billion of $64.60 billion in Q3 revenue. The new Class C structure is designed to keep Mark Zuckerberg in control, under a Founder Alignment Agreement.

stocks.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
stocks.overview: Alphabet owns Google Search, YouTube, Android, Google Cloud and the Gemini AI models, and sells its TPU AI chips through Google Cloud. Q3 2026 revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, Google Cloud revenue more than doubled (+103%) to $30.7 billion with $11.1 billion of operating income, and EPS was $2.12; the Gemini app has reached one billion users. This week Google announced a $15 billion data-center investment in Malaysia for 2027–2028 (Nov 4) and a $17 billion first data center in Laramie County, Wyoming (Nov 5), powered partly by a 702 MW Bloom fuel-cell system with carbon capture. Alphabet pays a $0.22 quarterly dividend on Dec 14 to holders of record on Dec 7. The main risk is legal: appeals are pending in both U.S. antitrust cases (search and ad tech), and a court refused to pause related private ad-tech suits.
stocks.researchSummary: Google Cloud is now Alphabet's fastest-growing engine, driven by AI infrastructure and TPU demand, and Google is committing tens of billions more to data centers even as U.S. local opposition grows. Antitrust remedies remain the key overhang.
stocks.cryptoLink: Google Cloud offers Universal Ledger, a managed, permissioned distributed ledger for tokenizing commercial bank money and securities and for wholesale payments.

flags.text: Google lost the U.S. DOJ and states' ad-tech antitrust case and is appealing. A court has denied its request to pause related private ad-tech suits while that appeal proceeds, according to MLex.

Political resistance to data centers is rising: Reuters, via Yahoo Finance, reports that all but one of 41 data-center ballot measures in this week's elections went against data centers, as Google commits $17 billion in Wyoming and $15 billion in Malaysia.
Google Search & other produced $63.35 billion of Alphabet's $127.58 billion Q3 revenue, so Search is still about half the business while Cloud scales.

stocks.name: NVIDIA Corporation
stocks.overview: Nvidia designs the GPUs, CPUs, networking and software that run most AI training and inference. In Q2 fiscal 2027 (to July 26, 2026) revenue rose 106% to $96.2 billion, data center revenue was $89.0 billion (+117%), gross margin was 75.0% and GAAP EPS was $2.46; Nvidia guided Q3 revenue to $108.0 billion ±2%, assuming no data-center compute revenue from China. Vera Rubin is in full production at CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, OCI and Nebius, and on Nov 6 Nvidia completed a $1 billion purchase of a 4.13% stake in Naver for a joint AI-factory venture in Korea. Nvidia reports Q3 FY27 results on Nov 17. The main risks are policy and AI-spending sentiment: shares fell more than 9% on Nov 5 amid post-midterm fears of an AI build-out slowdown, Democrats are preparing scrutiny of its chip exports, and on Nov 8 the board opened an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.
stocks.researchSummary: Nvidia's last reported quarter was another record, driven by data-center demand, and the Nov 17 report is the next major checkpoint. The backdrop has turned more complicated, with export-policy scrutiny and a board-led investigation announced Nov 8, though no wrongdoing has been established.

flags.text: Semafor reports that Democrats taking over regulatory committees, along with Republicans pushing stronger export controls, point to closer scrutiny of Nvidia's China chip sales, possibly through the lame-duck defense bill and Senate Banking under Sen. Warren.

Investors are questioning whether AI infrastructure growth can be sustained. Nvidia fell more than 9% on Nov 5, losing almost $450 billion in market cap, as fears of a post-election slowdown hit chip stocks.
Data center revenue was $89.0 billion of $96.2 billion in Q2 FY27 (about 93%), so results depend heavily on hyperscaler and AI-lab spending.
Board-led independent investigation announced Nov 8 after reports Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort; scope and timing not published.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
stocks.overview: AMD makes EPYC server CPUs, Instinct AI GPUs, Ryzen PC chips and embedded and gaming silicon. Q3 2026 revenue was a record $13.4 billion (+45%), data center revenue nearly doubled (+97%) to $8.5 billion on the MI450 launch and EPYC demand, and diluted EPS was $1.46 GAAP and $2.09 non-GAAP. Gaming revenue fell 40% to $773 million. AMD guided Q4 revenue to about $17 billion ±3% as it scales Helios rack systems and 'Venice' CPUs, and it filed its 10-Q on Nov 4. It is scheduled to present at the UBS conference on Dec 1 and Barclays on Dec 9. The main risk is AI-spending sentiment and supply: AMD shares fell double digits on Nov 5 in the post-midterm chip selloff, and the memory shortage is raising component costs.
stocks.researchSummary: AMD's latest quarter was its strongest on record and it is now mainly a data-center company, with guidance for faster growth in Q4. The stock's sharp drop on Nov 5 reflected sector-wide fears about the AI build-out rather than company-specific news.

flags.text: CNBC links the post-election chip selloff to concerns over data-center restrictions and power-cost rules: voters opposed data centers in all but one of 41 local ballot measures.

AMD competes with Nvidia in AI accelerators and with Intel in CPUs. CNBC notes that the global memory shortage is pushing up costs for AMD, Intel and Qualcomm, and AMD's gaming revenue fell 40% in Q3.
Data Center was $8.5 billion of $13.4 billion in Q3 revenue (about 64%), so AMD is increasingly tied to AI and cloud capex cycles.

stocks.name: Intel Corporation
stocks.overview: Intel designs and manufactures PC and server CPUs and is building a contract foundry business (Intel 14A). Q3 2026 revenue rose 21% to $16.5 billion, Data Center and AI revenue rose 78% to $7.3 billion (its strongest growth in 15 years) and Intel Foundry revenue rose 58%, with GAAP EPS of $0.60 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.52. Q4 guidance is $15.0–16.0 billion of revenue, with an expected PC slowdown through at least the first half of 2027. Recent deals include a multiyear Xeon collaboration with Oracle Cloud, a planned acquisition of Classiq (quantum software) and a $23 billion equity offering. CEO Lip-Bu Tan bought 150,000 shares on Nov 2 at about $64.73 (Form 4 filed Nov 4). The main risks are supply and execution: an accident at the Kiryat Gat fab in Israel will cost about $300 million of Q4 revenue, with a similar hit expected in Q1.
stocks.researchSummary: Intel's data-center demand is outrunning its supply, but a weaker PC outlook and the Israel fab accident produced soft guidance. The CEO's open-market purchase is a notable insider signal, though it is not a forecast.

flags.text: Intel lists the U.S. government's acquisition of significant equity interests in the company, along with export controls and trade policy, among its key risk factors.

Intel says demand for its data-center products 'continues to meaningfully exceed available supply', limited by Intel 3 yields, substrate shortages and the Fab 28 accident, which will cut about $300 million from Q4 revenue and 200 basis points from gross margin.

The turnaround rests on CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who has bought shares personally (150,000 on Nov 2). Client computing is still about half of Intel Products revenue ($8.1 billion of $15.4 billion), which leaves Intel exposed to the PC slowdown.

stocks.name: Amazon.com, Inc. (AWS)
stocks.overview: Amazon is the parent of AWS, the largest cloud provider, alongside its retail, Prime, advertising, devices and newer businesses (Zoox, Amazon Leo satellites, Pharmacy). In Q3 2026 AWS revenue rose 39% to $46.0 billion, its fastest growth in nearly five years and a $184 billion annualized run rate, with $17.8 billion of operating income (38.7% margin). Total net sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion, operating income was a record $28.1 billion and EPS was $1.89. AWS signed new agreements with Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Oracle and others, Bedrock token volume grew nearly 17x and Trainium became easier to adopt through TorchNeuron; CEO Andy Jassy projects AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. On Nov 5 Amazon launched $0 Uber Eats delivery for Prime members, and AWS re:Invent runs Nov 30–Dec 4 in Las Vegas. The main risk is capital intensity: 2026 cash capex of about $220 billion has pushed trailing free cash flow to an outflow of $42.4 billion.
stocks.researchSummary: AWS is accelerating on AI demand and is the main driver of Amazon's profits, while retail margins hit a record. The trade-off is very heavy AI capex funded partly with new debt, plus rising data-center permitting risk in the U.S.
stocks.cryptoLink: AWS stopped accepting new customers for Amazon Managed Blockchain (Ethereum, Bitcoin, Polygon node access) on Oct 29, 2026, and will end the service on Sep 29, 2027, pointing users to self-managed Node Runners on AWS or partners such as Alchemy and QuickNode.

flags.text: Voters sided against data centers in all but one of 41 local ballot measures on Nov 3, and CNBC reports that the hyperscalers, Amazon included, fell 2–4% on Nov 5 on build-out concerns.

Trailing-12-month free cash flow was an outflow of $42.4 billion and long-term debt rose to $173.1 billion from $65.6 billion at end-2025, as AWS competes with Google Cloud, whose revenue grew 103%, and Microsoft for AI capacity.
AWS generated $17.8 billion of Amazon's $28.1 billion Q3 operating income (about 63%), so group profit depends heavily on cloud and AI demand.
